ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the central carbon is connected to a negatively charged oxygen O⁻, an aryl Ar, a cyano group NC, and the adjacent carbon on the right; the adjacent carbon on the right is also connected to H, OH, and another Ar. The curved arrow shows the electron pair of O⁻ moving toward the central carbon to form C=O, while the bond electrons between the central carbon and the cyano group transfer onto the cyano group. Reasoning: After mechanically processing according to the arrow endpoints, the O–central carbon bond order increases to a carbonyl, the central carbon–cyano group bond breaks, and the cyano group obtains an electron pair to become [C-]#N. The remaining skeleton remains as a carbonyl carbon connected to one phenyl and one α-hydroxybenzyl fragment, i.e. an α-hydroxy ketone. Therefore the product SMILES is O=C(C(c1ccccc1)O)c2ccccc2.[C-]#N.

method.method_draft: Translate the image into the starting connectivity, then apply each arrow endpoint mechanically. Increase the O–central-C bond order to make a ketone, remove the central-C–cyanide bond, and assign the electron pair to cyanide as [C-]#N. Keep the adjacent carbon bonded to H, OH, and phenyl. Convert the resulting α-hydroxy ketone plus cyanide anion into SMILES: O=C(C(c1ccccc1)O)c2ccccc2.[C-]#N.

method.method_draft: Recognize the drawn species as the alkoxide form of a benzoin cyanohydrin. Collapse this cyanohydrin center to the corresponding α-hydroxy ketone: the carbon bearing O− becomes the carbonyl carbon, the CN group departs as cyanide anion, and the neighboring C bearing OH and phenyl remains attached to the carbonyl. With each Ar represented as phenyl, write the products as O=C(C(c1ccccc1)O)c2ccccc2 and [C-]#N, separated by a dot.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中是一个箭推机理片段，左侧中心碳连有 Ar、氰基/NC 取代基、带负电的 O⁻，并与右侧一个连有 Ar、H、OH 的碳相连；弯箭显示 O⁻ 的电子回推形成羰基，同时 C–CN 键的电子移向氰基使其离去。
再推理：按照该电子重排，原来带 O⁻ 的碳变为羰基碳，CN 作为氰ide 阴离子离去；相邻的带 OH、H 和 phenyl/Ar 的碳保持与羰基相连。因此产物是 α-羟基酮 benzoin 结构 PhC(=O)CH(OH)Ph 加氰ide 阴离子。对应 SMILES 为 O=C(C(c1ccccc1)O)c2ccccc2.[C-]#N。
